label: secondary
publisher_name: The New Yorker
authority_rationale: A magazine obituary reporting on Ginsburg's life and cancer history; it is not the court, Ginsburg herself, or her medical providers who originated the diagnosis information.

label: derived
publisher_name: World Bank (World Development Indicators data portal)
authority_rationale: The World Bank's population indicator compiles figures from the UN Population Division, national census offices, Eurostat and others, so it repackages third-party data rather than producing the 1960 Nigeria population estimate itself.
notes: The World Bank is an intergovernmental body, but for this indicator it acts as an aggregator. The page's source note credits the UN World Population Prospects and national statistical offices as the original producers. The archived page was judged as its original worldbank.org publisher.

label: primary
publisher_name: Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) and Bertelsmann Stiftung (SDG Index and Dashboards Report 2018)
authority_rationale: SDSN and Bertelsmann Stiftung compile and publish the SDG Index, so they are the original producers of Nigeria's 2018 ranking (150th of 156).
notes: The PDF is hosted on an Amazon S3 bucket named 'sustainabledevelopment.report', which appears to be the official storage behind the SDSN SDG report website. That makes it the producer's own infrastructure, not a third-party re-host. The report is primary for the 2018 ranking. Whether Nigeria 'performed poorly over five years' is an inference drawn from this and other years' data.

label: derived
publisher_name: PubMed Central (US National Library of Medicine, NIH), re-hosting a journal article by independent researchers
authority_rationale: The page is a PMC copy of a third-party systematic review, not original WHO material. The claim concerns what WHO said, so neither PMC nor the study authors are first-hand for that fact.
notes: The meta-analysis (Li et al., Am J Infect Control 2020) is original research on mask efficacy, so its own journal page would be primary only for background efficacy evidence, not for WHO's position. PMC hosting makes it derived either way.

label: primary
publisher_name: Congress.gov (Library of Congress, official legislative record of the U.S. Congress)
authority_rationale: Congress.gov is the official record of congressional legislation, so it is the first-hand source for whether H.Res.620 (116th Congress) was introduced and how far it advanced.
notes: The resolution is assumed to be the one the fact-checkers tied to the claim. The page excerpt was unavailable, but the URL identifies the official bill status page.

label: secondary
publisher_name: Library of Congress (Research Guides / Congress glossary)
authority_rationale: The Library of Congress glossary explains what a congressional resolution is. It does not record H. Res. 620 itself, so it is first-hand only for background and is an explainer relative to the claim.
notes: The Library of Congress is a legislative-branch agency, but this page is a general glossary, not the record of the resolution (that would be congress.gov). The label could be argued as derived, since it compiles definitions, but secondary/background fits best.

label: secondary
publisher_name: Insider (insider.com)
authority_rationale: A news outlet compiling photos and reports of orange skies from West Coast wildfire smoke; it reports on the phenomenon rather than being the authoritative originator of the fact.

label: secondary
publisher_name: Congressional Research Service (Library of Congress), via crsreports.congress.gov

notes: CRS is an official government body, but this Legal Sidebar (likely about the vacancy and nomination process) works as an explainer, not the originating record for her death or cancer history. The page content could not be checked; the judgement rests on the URL and the CRS product type.

label: unclear
publisher_name: Unknown Google Drive uploader
authority_rationale: The file is hosted on a generic Google Drive link with no title or text, so the uploader and producer of the document cannot be identified as the record-holder (e.g., IPID) for the police-killing and custody-death figures.
notes: It could be a copy of an IPID annual report or similar official statistics document. Even so, a Drive copy by an unknown party would be derived at best, and it would only be primary if uploaded by the producer itself, which cannot be verified.

label: secondary

authority_rationale: AP is a news agency reporting the Supreme Court's announcement of Ginsburg's death and its cause; the Court is the first-hand source.

label: primary

authority_rationale: The claim concerns what WHO says about masks, and this is WHO's own official Q&A page on its own domain stating its position, making it first-hand for the fact at issue.

label: primary
publisher_name: United Nations (Department of Economic and Social Affairs / UN Sustainable Development Goals site)
authority_rationale: The UN is the intergovernmental body that runs the SDG framework and produces the official annual SDG Progress Report, so it is a first-hand source on SDG progress measurement.
notes: This page is the global progress report overview and was cited for background on how the UN measures progress. It is not Nigeria-specific, so its first-hand authority covers SDG measurement generally rather than Nigeria's performance directly. Labelled primary because the UN is the originating producer of the SDG monitoring the claim relies on, but it is borderline.

label: secondary
publisher_name: UK Health Security Agency (formerly Public Health England) blog on blog.gov.uk
authority_rationale: The government health agency is first-hand only for background on the flu vaccination programme. It is not a source for the central fact, which is whether Sadiq Khan faked his flu jab with the needle cap on.
notes: For the background fact (flu deaths, vaccine eligibility) the publisher would be primary. Relative to the claim's central fact it has no first-hand role, so it is labelled secondary as context material. 'Unclear' was also considered since the page does not address the claim at all.

label: secondary
publisher_name: The Guardian (Poverty Matters blog, Global Development section)
authority_rationale: A news outlet writing about Nigeria's 50th independence anniversary; it neither produces nor officially records the 1960 independence date or the population figure.
notes: Cited only for background (the independence date), not the central population figure. Still journalism reporting historical facts, so secondary.

label: secondary
publisher_name: Biography.com (A&E Networks)
authority_rationale: Biography.com is an editorial biography and explainer site that summarizes RBG's career and health history from other sources. It is not the Supreme Court, the family, or the medical source of record, so it is not first-hand for her cancer history or her appointment.
notes: Borderline between secondary and derived. Biography.com is reference-like and encyclopedic in style, but it publishes original editorially written profiles rather than compiling or mirroring others' data, so secondary fits better.

label: secondary
publisher_name: Newsroom (newsroom.co.nz)
authority_rationale: Newsroom is a news outlet reporting on David Wong-Tung's directorships and defamation threat; it is not the companies register, Oravida, or Collins herself, so it is not first-hand for the Collins-Oravida connection.

publisher_name: Space Science and Engineering Center (SSEC), University of Wisconsin–Madison, JPSS Satellite Data Outreach & Calibration (SDOC) blog
authority_rationale: The page is a satellite-imagery blog post about the Australian Mallacoota fires. For the US orange/red sky claim it only provides explanatory background on smoke scattering, so it is not a first-hand source for the US sky observations.
notes: SSEC produces its own satellite imagery analysis, so it could count as primary for the Australian fire imagery. Relative to the US September 2020 claim, though, it serves as a scientific explainer about Mie scattering, not as a record of the event.

label: secondary
publisher_name: University of Wisconsin–Madison News (news.wisc.edu)
authority_rationale: A university news explainer on why the sky changes colour, quoting a meteorology professor; it gives general science background and is not a first-hand source for the September 2020 orange/red skies in the US.
notes: The university is an expert source for the science of light scattering, but this is background only, not the claim's central fact (the 2020 wildfire-smoke skies). The page reads as an institutional news explainer rather than original research.

label: secondary
publisher_name: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Nigeria
authority_rationale: UNDP Nigeria's page explains what the SDGs are, but it is not the source or record of Nigeria's SDG performance over the past five years, the central fact of the claim.
notes: UNDP is a UN body and first-hand for the general definition of the SDGs, which is the background question it was cited for. It holds no first-hand data on Nigeria's performance, so it is labelled as an explainer rather than primary for the claim.

label: primary
publisher_name: Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID), South Africa
authority_rationale: IPID is the statutory body that receives, records and investigates deaths caused by police action and deaths in police custody, so its annual report is the official first-hand source for these figures.
notes: This is an archived copy of IPID's own annual report on its own domain, so the archive is treated as transparent. The filename suggests the 2017(/18) report, while the claim refers to 2018. The reporting-year mismatch does not change who the publisher is.

publisher_name: electronic medicines compendium (emc), run by Datapharm
authority_rationale: emc re-hosts the manufacturer's regulator-approved Summary of Product Characteristics for the flu vaccine, giving only background on needle-cap removal, not first-hand evidence of whether Sadiq Khan faked his jab.
notes: The SmPC is produced by the vaccine manufacturer and approved by the MHRA. emc is a third-party compendium hosting these documents. The page is relevant only as background on administration procedure, not the claim's central fact.

label: secondary
publisher_name: National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD), South Africa
authority_rationale: The claim is about what the WHO says. The NICD is a South African public health agency, not the WHO, and this page relays the National Department of Health's mask recommendation rather than recording WHO's own statement.
notes: NICD is an official government body and is first-hand for South African mask guidance, but that is only context for the claim. It is not the holder of WHO's position, so it is not primary for the central fact.

authority_rationale: The ranking data were produced by the SDG Center for Africa and SDSN; sdgphilanthropy.org is a separate platform hosting a copy of their report, so it is a third-party re-hosted copy.
notes: The underlying report is the original data producer for the 2019 ranking (Nigeria 43 of 52), so it would be primary if hosted on sdgcafrica.org or sdgindex.org. The SDG Philanthropy Platform is a distinct initiative led by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors and UNDP, so this copy is treated as derived.

label: primary
publisher_name: UK Government (Department of Health and Social Care / MHRA) via GOV.UK
authority_rationale: The GOV.UK consultation document is the government's own proposal on changes to the Human Medicine Regulations (temporary authorisation of unlicensed COVID-19 vaccines, expanded workforce to administer them), which is the official source behind the claim.
notes: Archived via web.archive.org; judged as the original GOV.UK publisher. The consultation proposed that additional trained healthcare-related staff could administer vaccines. It did not propose employers doing so. It is still the first-hand source for the policy the claim distorts.

The image path is dated 2020/10/17 and sits in a Rockford folder, which suggests it may show the 17 Oct Janesville, WI rally rather than the 24 Oct Waukesha rally. An original press photo is direct visual evidence, but under these rules news outlets are labelled secondary.

authority_rationale: Santander's own official channel is a first-hand source on whether Santander itself was sending out new debit cards early, which is the company's own action.
